anchors: Pin each decision with a test that fails when the decision is reverted
decision: A hook records each choice a later editor could undo in a Decisions block in its module docstring, every entry pinned by a test that fails when the decision is reverted, and the block is read before a matcher, rule or threshold changes.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: hooks, jigs and scripts keep their reason in a Decisions block in the module docstring plus a regression test that goes red when the decision is reverted; no new file and no new gate for code

reopen_if: A hook decision is undone although its docstring entry and pinning test both carried it, or editors keep missing the block.
why: Hook rules were changed forward and back because the reason sat in a commit or a changelog the next editor never reads; the module and its tests are what that editor opens.

decision: Rejected: a decisions.jsonl ledger for hooks and jigs.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: skills get the ledger, code keeps its reason in the module docstring and a regression test; no new file and no new gate for code

reopen_if: a reverted code decision is found whose docstring and tests both carried it and it was still undone
why: code already carries its reason in the module docstring and its behaviour in a regression test; a second record would drift from both

anchors: Precision prices only a hazard a gate would block
decision: A guard against a wrong-answer hazard is priced by joining each firing to its tool result, not by guard_replay's precision.

evidence.text: Pricing a verdict-after-grep guard: 224 firings over 205,309 calls with gate precision meaningless; joining to outputs gave 2 verdicts beside a tool error and 22 with stderr suppressed.

reopen_if: guard_replay itself joins firings to outputs.
why: Such a hazard never produces a block, so precision reads 0 whatever the guard is worth.

anchors: Apply both to a new hook as a whole, and on an edit to an existing hook to the code the edit
decision: A hook whose handler logic is Python (a .py started through a launcher shim counts) is written and edited with coding-python-data-architecture and coding-python-performance-review: a new hook as a whole, an edit for the code the edit touches; handler logic in bash follows the two bash skills instead.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-16: Python jigs and tools are written with the data architecture and performance skills

reopen_if: One of the two skills is renamed or merged, or the user narrows or widens the scope (for example to every hook in the module's directory).
why: The questions asked before writing a hook covered the event, the matcher, the answer and the failure mode but not the handler's own code; a hook runs on every matching event, so its data shapes and per-call cost matter, and the two skills hold those rules.

anchors: a guard that must also cover a mod tool applies its rule inside the mod
decision: A tool a plugin mod registers gets no PreToolUse or PostToolUse event; a guard that must cover it applies its rule inside the mod.

evidence.text: headless probe on CLI 2.1.330: matcher Bash|mcp__bitranox__backlog_list|mcp__.* fired Pre and Post for Bash, never for the mod tool, which the transcript shows ran ok

reopen_if: a re-probe on a newer CLI shows a settings hook firing for a mod tool
why: a hook-only design silently leaves the mod tool unguarded with no error

decision: A mod's $.process.run subprocess has no CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; pass $.session.id() explicitly and test with the variable unset.

evidence.text: /proc/<pid>/environ of the claude process on CLI 2.1.330: no CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (HOME present as control); the Bash-tool child has it

reopen_if: the claude process itself starts carrying CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in its environment
why: code that looked the session up through the variable judged without the transcript, silently

anchors: Pair every pass test of a guard that reads a file with its liveness twin
decision: Quote the as_posix path in a Bash-tool test command, and pair every pass test of a file-reading guard with a refusal twin built the same way.

evidence.text: shlex.split of an unquoted Windows str(path) dropped the backslashes and split at a space; the quoted as_posix form parsed to one intact token

reopen_if: guards stop failing open on an unreadable file
why: a guard that cannot read the file fails open, so the pass test goes green exactly where the path broke
